title: The sign product squares to one
statement: Let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables and let $T \subseteq [n]$, and write $s(\rho, T) \in \bbr$ for the sign product of the bits that $\rho$ fixes on $T$, that is, the product over $i \in T$ of the $\pm 1$-encoding of $\rho$'s value at $i$. Being a product of values in $\{-1, 1\}$, it satisfies \[ s(\rho, T)^2 = 1. \]
hypotheses_covered: ρ is a restriction on n variables
replaced: For every restriction $\rho$ and every set $T \subseteq [n]$, $(\mathrm{signProd}\,\rho\,T)^2 = 1$.
